segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Hi Paul, Derek Shaw from Brinewatch, thanks for jumping on. So um, I'll just give you the quick rundown of what we do because I think you're going to love it. We put wireless temperature sensors in coolers, freezers and trucks and the second anything drifts, the right person gets a text. We've got dashboards, reports, a mobile app, the works and our customers tell us it pays for itself in the first year.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Okay, we don't have trucks though. It's just the hospital kitchen.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Totally totally that's fine, the kitchen's actually our sweet spot, how many coolers and freezers.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Four walk-ins and about twenty reach-ins across the kitchen and the patient floors.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Perfect. So every one of those gets a sensor and you'd see them all on one screen, and the reports are great for inspections because everything's timestamped automatically and you can export it with one click, plus the alerts escalate so if the first person doesn't respond it goes to the next.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: That would help right now the walk-in alarms only beep in the kitchen. Last month one went off at night and nobody heard it until the morning shift.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Oh yeah, that's exactly the kind of thing we fix all

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: And we lost a whole cooler of patient meals. Our accreditation survey is coming up too, and they always pull the temperature logs.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Right, right, well, the logs would be automatic so that's covered. Our setup takes about a day and we handle everything. We also have a great integration with most facility systems and you can set up as many users as you want.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: How does it connect? Our IT department is pretty strict about devices on the hospital network.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: It's all cellular so it doesn't touch your network at all. It usually loves that part.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Good, because that would have been the first question.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: So what I'll do is send over our standard proposal for the 4 walk-ins and the 20 reach-ins and you can take a look. Sound good?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Sure, send it over and I'll look at it.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Awesome I'll get that to you today, great talking Paul.

reply: {"strengths":[{"text":"You adapted when Paul ruled out trucks and asked for the equipment count to scope the kitchen.","segment":"s02-s003","quote":"how many coolers and freezers."},{"text":"You answered the network concern directly and clearly.","segment":"s02-s012","quote":"It's all cellular so it doesn't touch your network at all."},{"text":"You connected automatic logs to the inspection need Paul raised.","segment":"s02-s010","quote":"the logs would be automatic so that's covered."}],"improvements":[{"text":"Open with a discovery question instead of a product rundown; your 18-second monologue and 69% talk share suggest more room for Paul to talk.","segment":"s02-s001","quote":"I'll just give you the quick rundown of what we do"},{"text":"When Paul shared the lost cooler and upcoming survey, ask about the impact and his current process before saying it's covered; you asked only one question on the call.","segment":"s02-s010","quote":"the logs would be automatic so that's covered."},{"text":"Before sending a standard proposal, clarify Paul's timing and what he'll need to decide; the call ended without that discovery.","segment":"s02-s014","quote":"send over our standard proposal"}]}
